message.content:
Below is a concise summary of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is not legal advice; if you need help with a specific situation, consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit. | Keep a written receipt and take photos of the unit before moving in. | | **Move‑in Inspection** | You should receive a written move‑in inspection report. | Review it carefully; note any existing damage and get the landlord to sign it. | | **Habitability** | Landlords must keep the premises safe, sanitary, and in good repair (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical). | Report problems promptly in writing. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenants; 60‑day notice for longer leases. | Keep copies of all notices sent/received. | | **Eviction Process** | Evictions must follow the Texas Property Code §92.001–92.004. A landlord must file a complaint in court and obtain a judgment before a sheriff can enforce removal. | If you receive a notice, respond in writing and consider contacting a lawyer or tenant‑rights group. | | **Rent Increases** | No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | Verify the notice period in your lease. | | **Discrimination** | Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Civil Rights Code, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, family status, or source of income. | Keep records of any discriminatory actions. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | Landlords must allow you to live without unreasonable interference. | Document any disturbances (e.g., excessive noise, entry without notice). | | **Repair and Deduct** | If the landlord fails to fix major repairs after notice, you may repair them yourself and deduct the cost from rent (but only if the repair is necessary for health/safety). | Get receipts and keep a record of communication. | | **Lease Termination** | You can terminate a lease early if the landlord breaches the lease or fails to maintain the property. | Provide written notice and keep copies. | | **Subletting** | Subletting is allowed unless prohibited by the lease. | Obtain written permission if required. | | **Utilities** | Landlords must provide hot water, heat, and electricity. | Check utility bills and confirm service is active. | | **Landlord Entry** | Landlords must give at least 24 hours written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | Keep a log of entries. | | **Record Keeping** | Maintain copies of all lease documents, receipts, correspondence, and photographs. | Store them in a safe place. | ### Resources | Resource | What it offers | How to access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Tenant‑rights guides, dispute resolution services | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov | | **Texas Tenants Association** | Legal assistance, workshops, advocacy | https://www.texastenants.org | | **Local County Clerk’s Office** | Filing complaints, eviction notices | Visit your county clerk’s website | | **Legal Aid of North Texas** | Free legal help for low‑income residents | https://legalaidnt.org | | **National Apartment Association** | National resources, local chapters | https://www.naahq.org | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Get a written lease** – read it thoroughly. 2. **Take a photo walk-through** – document condition. 3. **Ask about security deposit** – confirm amount and return policy. 4. **Know your notice periods** – both for paying rent and ending tenancy. 5. **Keep all communication in writing** – email or certified mail. If you encounter a problem—such as a landlord refusing to make repairs, unlawful eviction notice, or discrimination—contact a local tenant‑rights organization or an attorney right away.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. But we might also offer to generate a contract. The user didn't ask for a contract. So we just answer. No tool needed. Provide overview: security deposit limits, notice requirements, habitability, eviction process, etc. Also mention resources.
